They listen, answer every question, and make sure I understand what is going on and feel comfortable with the care he is receiving.
What means the most to me is that their concern for him feels genuine. They know him, they care about how he is doing, and they treat him with the same tenderness and compassion that I would hope anyone caring for a beloved pet would have.

I needed a refresher for my cats' rabies vaccination and called. In a very friendly conversation I got an appointment and was asked to prepay the visit for both, resulting in paying $150. During the conversation I explicitly stated that I simply want the rabies vaccination, nothing more.

Upon arrival all was as you'd expect from a friendly veterinary clinic. After assessment my cats got vaccinated. I was a bit puzzled by the use of two syringes per cat and asked about that. I was informed that it's easier for the cats with two shots. I was not informed that they got an additional vaccination that I did not ask for.

After the treatment, I was ushered into payment in the treatment room, not at the counter what I expected. The screen that I tapped had no itemized invoice, just $120. I paid, without even having seen the invoice, stupid me. Only at home I learned that my cats got treatment that I didn't ask for and, more importantly, did not consent to. In addition to the rabies vaccine they got FVRR-CP.

That feels like misrepresentation, and my attorney considers that to be breach of consumer protection if not more severe. I'm just happy that my company records all phone calls and I have a witness. And I'm considering legal steps.

Did anyone had a similar experience? I really would like to know.

It's a pity.

The front desk hasn’t been the most attentive when both my mother and I have been there to receive the services that we need for our pet. It’s more like we have to present ourselves instead of the other way around.  Even Service workers, are taught to greet people as soon as they come in.

Both the tech and the doctor seemed dismissive of how fearful my dog was and laughed at her instead of trying to get her on the table, which I had to do so myself.

In doing so, my dog peed on the table and instead of wiping it down before putting her on her side, they decided with their years of medical knowledge that, It’s OK to have her stink like piss after her appointment.

Honestly, I’m not even sure if what they gave my dog was even needed because it really went away on its own. Maybe it’s some BS that they sold us and that’s why the doctor is in such a low mood because their sales are bad or they need to push their inventory onto customers. I don’t know.

And I hope y’all don’t respond with any BS like “call us so we can make this right”. Y’all can hire better receptionists, and the doctor can retire since it seems like her heart isn’t in the business. That would make things right in my eyes.

Y’all are right down the street, literally walking distance.
I much rather drive 30 minutes for the bare minimum treatment and more for my dog.

Reply to BS Reply:

Of course this isn’t my real name. Chances were given already to rectify behavior everyday for years and yet nothing has. Self awareness of behaviors is a difficult task, especially if it’s a habit that requires low effort like ignoring people when they come in and dismissing living being’s fear.

Thank you for showing my dog and I what mistreatment is like so that I can recognize being snubbed at other places and leave ASAP.

Be cautious if your pet needs a prescription diet. While Dr. Kurtz is kind and I've had positive experiences with her (which is the only reason I am not giving a 1 star review), her office manager has proven to be difficult and rude. My cat requires medication for life as well as veterinary prescription food and it is very expensive. Their "policy" is that you have to order from their pharmacy or come and pick up a prescription - they will not email it to you (which makes no sense other than to make it difficult if you want to order food from Chewy which has no delivery fees). I had eye surgery, couldn't drive, and begged them to email me a prescription for a bag of treats to make it easier to give my very hard to medicate cat what he needed (an issue both Dr. Kurtz  and her office manger are well aware of). I emailed them a photo of my swollen, bandaged eyes so they wouldn't think I was being dishonest. I was told the office manager would call me back and she did not. I also don't have a scanner so I had to wait 5 days until I could drive again, get the prescription, and go to a UPS store to scan it. When I picked it up, I sarcastically thanked the office manger for not calling me back and she gave me a smirky smile and said "You're so welcome." I order plenty of medication from their pharmacy as well as buying food on-site, and would have had no problem ordering the treats from them if they didn't charge $14.95 for shipping an $8.00 bag of cat treats. Was really taken aback by how I was ignored and subsequently treated so obnoxiously.

Briar Grove Animal Clinic is, without a doubt, one of the best--if not the best--veterinary practices in Houston. I've been a loyal client for some time now, and there's no place I would trust more with the care of my pets. From every angle, they consistently exceed my expectations. The team of doctors is nothing short of exceptional, led by the incredibly knowledgeable Dr. Kurtz, the clinic's owner, who is deeply committed to ensuring the health and well-being of every animal under their care. While all the veterinarians here are outstanding, what truly sets them apart is how they treat each animal as if it were their own beloved pet. To me, that's the most important quality to seek in a vet. The support staff--techs and front desk personnel--are equally attentive and helpful, always going the extra mile to make sure both pets and owners feel comfortable and cared for. I have four cats and one dog, and recently had to make the heart-wrenching decision to say goodbye to one of my dogs. Throughout this difficult time, the doctors were compassionate and kept me fully informed, allowing me the space I needed to grieve and cherish my final moments with my pet. Additionally, I have a tendency to rescue and foster animals, including tiny, bottle-fed babies. Briar Grove has been an invaluable partner in providing expert care and guidance as I care for these little ones. I truly cannot recommend this clinic enough. If I could rate them higher, I absolutely would. As long as I'm in Houston, I'll be a loyal client, and I enthusiastically recommend them to friends, family--and now, to you, dear internet strangers.
